llm.summary: The skill's stated purpose (local BLE control of a Venus vibrator) matches its instructions, but it tells you to clone and run code from an untrusted GitHub repository and execute arbitrary local scripts — a proportionate but risky install pattern that requires manual review before use.

dimensions.detail: Name/description match the implementation: the skill only describes calling a local HTTP bridge that broadcasts BLE commands on macOS. No unrelated cloud services, credentials, or system-wide configuration are requested.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The SKILL.md instructs the user (and the agent) to git clone a third‑party repo, run Python scripts (sniff_cachito.py, server.py, ble_worker.py), and edit ble_worker.py to embed a device_id. Those steps are necessary for the stated purpose but they expand the scope to downloading and executing arbitrary code and modifying local files — actions that should be audited before running.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no formal install spec, but the runtime flow requires cloning https://github.com/AmandaClarke61/toybrige and running its scripts (via 'uv sync' and 'uv run'). Downloading and executing code from an untrusted personal GitHub repo and running dependency tooling (uv) is moderate-to-high risk unless the repository is verified.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requests no environment variables or credentials. It does require macOS Bluetooth permissions and local file edits (DEVICE_ID) which are proportional to controlling a Bluetooth toy.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always is false and the skill is user-invocable. It does not request persistent system privileges or claim to modify other skills or global agent config.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to do what it claims, but it requires you to clone and run code from an unverified GitHub repo and execute local Python scripts that access your Mac's Bluetooth. Before installing or running it: (1) inspect server.py and ble_worker.py in the repository for network calls, telemetry, or unexpected commands; (2) prefer to fork the repo and review its commit history or use a repository from a trusted author; (3) run the server in an isolated environment (separate account, VM, or disposable Mac) until you’re confident it only binds to localhost and not to external endpoints; (4) avoid running it on sensitive machines and do not provide credentials — none are required; (5) verify the repo URL and spelling (toybrige vs toybridge) to avoid typosquatting; (6) be aware of privacy/consent implications when controlling a personal device. If you cannot audit the code or run it safely in isolation, treat the skill as potentially unsafe.
